round1_to_round2.summary: The forecasters converged. The fair-value spread narrowed from $550-582 to $550-585 and the mean rose from $568 to $571. All five now use FY27 EPS of $15.58, an NTM EPS of about $19.3-20.4 at Sep-2027, ~30x (agent_3 uses 29x), 3.9-4.5% dilution (first-GW warrant tranches plus ~13.6M World Labs shares) and ~$9.9B net cash. The mean P(close >= spot) moved from 0.484 to 0.49, and the round-1 supervisor ladder was 0.494. Agent_5 (+$23, dropped its inconsistent EV/sales leg) and agent_4 (-$13, added dilution) moved the most. Agent_3 held at $550: removing the stale delay leg lifted its value, but a stricter NTM framing and a ~$3/share customer-financing cost offset that. All five fair values sit 3-9% below the $604.09 spot. This is still one shared 30x de-rating judgment, not five independent confirmations.

revision_check.note: It corrected the warrant-vesting fact (the GW milestones bind, not the $600 price test), added the $4.1B lease guarantees to its bear case, and put ~28% on an in-window Q3 print in its 1-month ladder. It kept its FV at $580, its 12-month ladder and its $380 thesis break, and explained why. The unchanged ladder is defensible because it was already near the corrected centre. Its median (~$607) sits above its own $580 FV and its upper tail is the fattest of the five (0.06 at $1,510). That is a judgment on drift, not an error.

It rebuilt dilution with explicit tranche probabilities (~50M warrant shares + 13.6M World Labs, 3.9%) and moved its 2027 revenue to the $88.1B consensus. Its EV/sales leg at 10x on ~$102B NTM implies ~31x its own NTM earnings, so the two legs are consistent. It added the FOMC and Micron (Micron reports FQ4 after the close on Sep 30, so the reaction lands Oct 1, inside the window). It kept its $360 thesis break with a reason. A good in-lane revision.

It dropped the stale Helios-slip leg and fixed net cash ($9.9B) and the multiple framing (~39x FY27 / ~42x NTM). It added World Labs, and it rebuilt the skeptic case on primary 10-Q customer-financing disclosures, which I verified. It holds $550 through 29x and a ~$3/share financing cost. That is a disclosed judgment, not an error. Round-2 research was thin (one 10-Q fetch, three searches), but it was primary and in lane.

It applied 4.5% dilution, counted both warrants, made EV/sales (9.5x, ~30x implied earnings) consistent, and dropped the X post and the content-farm sources. It still uses ~$15B forward net cash in its EV/sales leg without netting the up-to-$5.0B post-quarter investment commitments, which cost about $1/share at its 30% weight. Minor.

It fixed the EV/sales inconsistency (7.5x to 10x), added dilution and net cash, and flagged FY28 EPS as derived. Its NTM revenue of ~$95B at Sep-2027 is still low against its own path: FY27 consensus is $88.1B, and ~38% EPS growth in FY28 implies ~$100-105B NTM revenue. On ~$102B its EV/sales leg would be ~$590, not $553, which lifts its FV about $9 to ~$582. It left its 1-month ladder unchanged, which is fine because it already carried the in-window earnings risk in round 1.

disagreements.positions: agent_3 charges ~$3/share (~$5B) expected cost for $4.1B lease guarantees, $5.0B investment commitments, $9.5B of new data-center leases and $30.3B of purchase commitments, and adds partner default to its thesis break. agent_1 puts the guarantees (~$2.5/share max) in the bear case only. agents 2, 4 and 5 do not price them.
disagreements.resolution: The figures are real and primary. The trend matters more than the level. The $4.1B guarantee exposure is unchanged from Q1 (Mar 28 10-Q: $4.1B, the same wording). Its fair value is recorded as 'not material', and one known instance is the ~$300M Crusoe loan backstop (Feb 2026). Purchase commitments rose from $25.7B to $30.3B (+18% q/q) with revenue guided +13% q/q. These are mostly wafers, substrates and components, plus multi-year cloud-service arrangements, so they are normal for a business heading to ~$88B of revenue. The new step is post-quarter: up to $5.0B of investment commitments through FY2028 and $9.5B of lease payments over up to 16 years starting 2027-28, against only $4.5B of not-yet-commenced leases at June 27. In total that is ~$18.6B gross (~$11/share, ~2% of market cap) if everything went to zero at once. The expected cost is ~$2-4/share: ~10% loss on the guarantees, a partial haircut on equity stakes in customers, and lease costs of ~$0.6-0.9B/yr from 2027-28 that may or may not be offset by revenue. agent_3's ~$3/share is reasonable. The bigger point is that the exposure is correlated with the AI-capex bear case, where partners default exactly when GPU demand falls. It therefore fattens the left tail a little and does not move the median. It is AMD copying Nvidia's vendor-financing playbook at a smaller scale, not a hidden balance-sheet hole.
disagreements.evidence: AMD 10-Q Q2 2026 (Note 8 Lease Guarantees; MD&A Financial Condition: $30.3B unconditional commitments, $17.4B for rest of FY26; subsequent-event $5.0B investment commitments and $9.5B leases); AMD 10-Q Q1 2026 ($4.1B guarantees, $25.7B commitments, $4.4B not-yet-commenced leases); DCD/The Information (Feb 2026) on AMD's ~$300M Crusoe loan backstop.

disagreements.topic: Is there an edge vs the $604.09 spot?
disagreements.positions: Fair values: agent_1 $580, agent_2 $585, agent_3 $550, agent_4 $569, agent_5 $573 (mean $571), 3-9% below spot. Ladders put P(close >= 604) at 0.47-0.51 (mean 0.49), with medians ~$590-607.
disagreements.resolution: No actionable edge. The whole gap to spot sits inside the shared multiple assumption: each 1x of forward P/E is ~$19/share, so 31.5x instead of 30x erases it. After the agent-level fixes (agent_5's NTM revenue, agent_4's forward net cash, a ~$3 financing cost for everyone), the reconciled FV is ~$577, 4.5% below spot. Against 72% realized volatility (a 1-sd 12-month move of about +/-$430), a 4.5% gap is noise. The ladder medians are a little above the fair values because agents allow some drift and a right-skewed bull case. That is consistent, not a contradiction.

A close there would most likely mean the guided 2027 data-center doubling has failed and not just volatility: a Helios/MI450 volume ramp that misses the Q4 and Q1'27 step-ups, cuts to the OpenAI/Meta/Anthropic first-GW deployments, a 2027 hyperscaler capex reset, or a commercial partner default that calls AMD's lease guarantees and impairs its customer investments.

Valuation already prices consensus: ~39x FY27 / ~42x NTM. All five forecasters assume de-rating to ~29-30x NTM, and each 1x is ~$19/share, so the ~4.5% gap to spot is within the error of that assumption.
Dilution of ~4-4.5% by the horizon (first-GW tranches of the 320M $0.01 OpenAI/Meta warrants plus ~13.6M World Labs shares) is outside consensus EPS.

Vendor financing is growing: $4.1B lease guarantees (flat since Q1), $30.3B purchase commitments (up from $25.7B), and after quarter-end up to $5.0B of investment commitments and $9.5B of new data-center leases. The expected cost is small (~$2-4/share), but it deepens a capex downturn.

fair_value.reason: NTM non-GAAP EPS at Sep-2027 ~$20 (0.25 x $15.58 FY27 + 0.75 x ~$21.5 FY28) x 30x = ~$600, /1.045 for expected warrant and World Labs dilution = ~$574, + ~$6/share net cash ($13.1B cash and ST investments vs $3.25B debt) = ~$580, less ~$3/share expected cost of the customer-financing stack (guarantee losses, haircut on customer investments, unrecovered lease cost) = ~$577. This corrects agent_5's low NTM revenue (its FV would be ~$582) and agent_4's forward net cash that ignores the investment commitments (~$568). It keeps 30x rather than agent_3's 29x. The agents' mean is $571.4. At ~4.5% below spot, fair value sits well within the ~$19/share-per-turn uncertainty of the shared multiple.

summary: In round 2 the five forecasters converged on $550-585 fair value (mean $571), using the same inputs: FY27 EPS $15.58, NTM ~$20, ~30x, ~4-4.5% dilution and $9.9B net cash. The ladders put P(close >= $604 spot) at ~0.49. The customer-financing exposure agent_3 raised is real but modest. The $4.1B lease guarantees have been flat since Q1. The new post-quarter $5.0B investment and $9.5B lease commitments cost ~$2-4/share in expectation and mainly deepen the left tail in an AI-capex downturn. My reconciled fair value is ~$577, 4.5% below spot and within the ~$19/share-per-turn error of the shared multiple, so there is no edge in either direction and the forecasters' mean ladder stands (low confidence).
